title: Motion in 2D — Projectile Motion: Standard Model and Modified-Dynamics Demand
subject: Physics

learner_defaults.interpretation: Routing coordinate only; it does not change Core1A/Core1B coverage or establish mastery.

diagnostic.prompt: At one instant, x-motion gives t=2 s. May the y equation use t=3 s for the same particle state?
diagnostic.answer: No. Independent components use separate axis equations but one shared physical time.

diagnostic.prompt: A projectile is at its apex. Which quantity is zero: total velocity, horizontal velocity, or vertical velocity?
diagnostic.answer: Only the vertical velocity component is zero in the standard no-drag projectile model.

diagnostic.prompt: If a force proportional to velocity acts during flight, may the ordinary constant-acceleration projectile equations be used unchanged?
diagnostic.answer: No. First decide the modified force model; velocity-dependent drag makes acceleration non-constant.

demands.bottleneck_decision: Use instantaneous velocity components from derivatives, not the position-vector direction.
demands.assumed_prerequisite: Signed x/y components and introductory derivative-as-rate meaning.
demands.canonical_part: One object, independent x/y components, one shared clock, velocity direction from signed components.
demands.extension_part: Differentiate x(t) and y(t) to obtain the simultaneous velocity components.

other_candidate_refs.reason_not_selected: The 2023 item is a building/slide projectile with a stated coefficient of restitution and multiple statements; it does not match the owner demand of a 45-degree projectile losing half its kinetic energy at the first ground bounce and leaving at 30 degrees.

demands.bottleneck_decision: Convert the retained kinetic-energy fraction into a speed-squared fraction before resolving the rebound direction.
demands.assumed_prerequisite: Standard projectile height relation and velocity components.
demands.canonical_part: After impact creates a new launch state, the rise to the new apex is gravity-only projectile motion.
demands.extension_part: Impact energy loss determines the post-impact speed before the canonical projectile model can restart.

demands.bottleneck_decision: Preserve the apex state and apply the changed gravity only to the post-apex stage.
demands.assumed_prerequisite: Apex condition v_y=0 and constant-acceleration fall from a known height.
demands.canonical_part: Each constant-g segment still uses componentwise constant acceleration and one shared clock.
demands.extension_part: The acceleration law changes at a boundary, so the trajectory is piecewise rather than one standard projectile.

demands.bottleneck_decision: Use the trajectory relation for point membership, then separately decide whether the point is before or after the apex.
demands.assumed_prerequisite: Standard projectile component equations and algebraic elimination of a common variable.
demands.canonical_part: The path follows from the gravity-only component equations sharing one time.
demands.extension_part: Eliminate time to obtain y(x), impose the point, and use velocity/slope for branch classification.

demands.bottleneck_decision: Reject constant horizontal velocity because linear drag makes a_x depend on v_x, then integrate exponential v_x(t).
demands.assumed_prerequisite: Newton's second law in one component and exponential decay supplied or previously bridged.
demands.canonical_part: The x/y component split and one common clock remain valid.
demands.extension_part: The acceleration is velocity-dependent, so the canonical constant-acceleration law is no longer valid on the dragged axis.

MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-INDEPENDENT-COMPONENTS.problem: A particle has v_x=6 m/s and v_y=-8 m/s at t=3 s. What makes these components one physical state?
route: Keep the same t=3 s for both components.
MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-INDEPENDENT-COMPONENTS.result: The state is v=(6,-8) m/s at one shared instant.

MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-CONSTANT-ACCELERATION.problem: With u=(4,6) m/s and a=(0,-2) m/s², find v after 2 s.

MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL.problem: A ball is released into free flight with u_x=8 m/s and u_y=6 m/s. State the acceleration model.
MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL.result: The gravity-only projectile model is licensed.

MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-VEL-FROM-POSITION.problem: For x=4t and y=10t-t², find v at t=2 s.

MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJ-BOUNCE-ENERGY.problem: A rebound retains 49% of kinetic energy. What fraction of the pre-impact speed remains?
route: Take the positive square root of 0.49.

MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJ-PIECEWISE-G.problem: From the same apex height, gravity doubles after the apex. How does descent time change?
route: Preserve the apex height and v_y=0.
MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJ-PIECEWISE-G.result: The descent time becomes 1/sqrt(2) of the ordinary value.

MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJ-TRAJECTORY-POINT.problem: For theta=45°, what extra test tells whether a known point on the path is after the apex?
route: Use the path equation for membership.
Check v_y or dy/dx at the point.
MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJ-TRAJECTORY-POINT.result: A negative vertical velocity or slope places the point after the apex.

MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-LINEAR-DRAG.problem: If m/c=3 s, what fraction of initial horizontal speed remains after 3 s?

visual_specs.purpose: Separate the position ray from the tangent velocity direction.
visual_specs.alt: A curved trajectory with a point P, a ray from the origin to P, and a distinct tangent velocity arrow at P.

visual_specs.purpose: Show impact as a boundary and the new launch state after energy loss.
visual_specs.alt: Incoming projectile arc reaches the ground, an impact boundary is marked with retained kinetic-energy fraction f, then a new rebound velocity points upward toward a lower apex.

visual_specs.purpose: Show the apex boundary between two constant-gravity stages.
visual_specs.alt: Projectile rises under g1 to an apex boundary and descends under g2, with the apex position and velocity carried across.

visual_specs.purpose: Bind a specified point to the path and show a local tangent for branch classification.
visual_specs.alt: Coordinate axes with a parabolic projectile path, marked point P, apex, and local tangent at P.

visual_specs.purpose: Contrast constant horizontal speed with exponential decay under linear drag.
visual_specs.alt: Graph of horizontal velocity against time starting at v_x0 and decaying exponentially, with time constant m/c marked.
